translation_notes: no island opportunity in this region: it builds an empty Dataset and parses TriG text obtained from a file, so translated.ldpy is the Python source verbatim (ldpy is a superset of Python). The prefix declarations the draft inserted were unused — and had been spliced into the middle of the `from nanopub import (` statement, which does not parse — so they were removed

the nanopub URI 'http://purl.org/np/RA1sViVmXf-...' stays a Python string on both sides: it is passed to a str-typed lookup API and compared with `np.source_uri`, a str; an `<...>` island would make it a URIRef, and rdflib's URIRef never compares equal to a plain str

context (driver-side, identical for both representations): the nanopub package is not installed in the venv, so the corpus checkout Nanopublication/nanopub-py@05022dc4bc is put on sys.path before either module is executed; original.py itself is unmodified

context: the region's `testsuite` fixture normally downloads the nanopub test suite from GitHub at import time. The single entry it needs, valid/trusty/example4.trig from Nanopublication/nanopub-testsuite@main (MIT), was copied into the example directory and is served by a stand-in defined in driver.py
equivalence is therefore trivial here (the two files are byte-identical); the driver still executes both sides end to end, including the in-test assertions
